title: ratelimit Module
content_markdown: This module implements rate limiting for SIP requests. In contrast to the PIKE module this limits the flow based on a per SIP request type basis and not per source IP. The latest sources allow you to dynamically group several messages into some entities and limit the traffic based on them. The MI interface can be used to change tunables while running OpenSIPS.
overview: This module implements rate limiting for SIP requests. In contrast to the PIKE module this limits the flow based on a per SIP request type basis and not per source IP. The latest sources allow you to dynamically group several messages into some entities and limit the traffic based on them. The MI interface can be used to change tunables while running OpenSIPS.
how_it_works:
This module is integrated with the OpenSIPS Key-Value Interface, providing support for distributed rate limiting using Redis or Memcached CacheDB backends. The internal limiting data will no longer be kept on each OpenSIPS instance. It will be stored in the distributed Key-Value database and queried by each instance before deciding if a SIP message should be blocked or not.

To achieve a distributed ratelimit feature, the module can also replicate its pipes counters to different OpenSIPS instances using the clusterer module. To do that, define the _pipe\_replication\_cluster_ parameter in your configuration script.

Starting with OpenSIPS 3.2, choosing whether to replicate a pipe over CacheDB backends or bin replication is triggered by the flags specified when the pipe is created: adding the _/r_ suffix to the pipe's name will replicate through CacheDB, and adding _/b_ will replicate through bin/clusterer.

exported_parameters.name: timer_interval
exported_parameters.description: The timer interval in seconds when the Network and Feedback algorithms run their queries, and the other algorithms reset their counters.
exported_parameters.notes: A too small value may lead to performance penalties due to timer process overloading.

exported_parameters.name: limit_per_interval
exported_parameters.description: This parameter configures the way that a pipe's limit is specified in the _rl\_check_ function and only affects the Taildrop and RED algorithms. A value of 1 means that the limit is set per-_timer\_interval_ while a value of 0 means per-second.

exported_parameters.name: expire_time
exported_parameters.description: This parameter specifies how long a pipe should be kept in memory after it becomes idle (no more operations are performed on the pipe) until deleted.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: The size of the hash table internally used to keep the pipes. A larger table is much faster but consumes more memory. The hash size must be a power of 2 number.

exported_parameters.name: default_algorithm
exported_parameters.description: Specifies which algorithm should be assumed in case it isn't explicitly specified in the _rl\_check_ function.

exported_parameters.name: cachedb_url
exported_parameters.description: Enables distributed rate limiting and specifies the backend that should be used by the CacheDB interface.

exported_parameters.name: db_prefix
exported_parameters.description: Specifies what prefix should be added to the pipe name. This is only used when distributed rate limiting is enabled.

exported_parameters.name: repl_buffer_threshold
exported_parameters.description: Used to specify the length of the buffer used by the binary replication, in bytes, when a flush should be performed - the pipes gathered until then should be sent on the network. This is used to avoid using large amount of memory for pipes replication.

exported_parameters.name: repl_timer_interval
exported_parameters.description: Timer in milliseconds, used to specify how often the module should replicate its counters to the other instances.

exported_parameters.name: repl_timer_expire
exported_parameters.description: Timer in seconds, used to specify when the counter received from a different instance should no longer be taken into account. This is used to prevent obsolete values, in case an instance stops replicating its counters.

exported_parameters.name: pipe_replication_cluster
exported_parameters.description: Specifies the cluster ID where pipes will be replicated to and received from.

exported_parameters.name: window_size
exported_parameters.description: How long the history in SBT should be in seconds.

exported_parameters.name: slot_period
exported_parameters.description: Value of one slot in milliseconds. This parameter determines how granular the algorithm should be. The number of slots will be determined by window\_size/slot\_period.
exported_parameters.example_code:
modparam("ratelimit", "window\_size", 5)
#we will have 50 slots of 100 milliseconds
modparam("ratelimit", "slot\_period", 100)

exported_functions.name: rl_check

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: this is the name that identifies the pipe which should be checked. One can also specify the _/s_ suffix to indicate the pipe should be replicated over cached, or _/b_ to replicate over bin/clusterer interface.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: this specifies the threshold limit of the pipe. It is strongly related to the algorithm used. Note that the limit should be specified as per-second, not per-timer_interval.

parameters.name: algorithm
parameters.description: this parameter reffers to the algorithm used to check the pipe. If it is not set, the default value is used.

return_values.condition: if the limit for the matched pipe is reached

exported_functions.description:
Check the current request against the pipe identified by name and changes/updates the limit. If no pipe is found, then a new one is created with the specified limit and algorithm, if specified. If the algorithm parameter doesn't exist, the default one is used.

NOTE: A pipe's algorithm cannot be dynamically changed. Only the one specified when the pipe was created will be considered.

NOTE: This function increments the pipe's counter every time it is called, even if the call should be declined. Therefore If you are using ratelimit to limit only successful traffic, you need to explicitely decrease the counter for the declined calls using the _rl_dec_count()_ function.

examples.description: perform a pipe match for all INVITE methods using RED algorithm
use default algorithm for each different gateway

exported_functions.name: rl_dec_count

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: identifies the name of the pipe.

exported_functions.description: This function decreases a counter that could have been previously increased by _rl_check_ function.

exported_functions.name: rl_reset_count

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: identifies the name of the pipe.

exported_functions.description: This function resets a counter that could have been previously increased by _rl_check_ function.

exported_functions.name: rl_values

parameters.name: ret_avp
parameters.description: an AVP where the pipes' names will be stored.

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: a regular expression used to filter the names of the pipes. If missing, all the pipes are returned.

exported_functions.description: Returns all the available pipes' names in the _ret_avp_ output variable.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_list

parameters.name: pipe
parameters.description: indicates the name of the single pipe to be listed.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: a pattern used to filter the active pipes to be listed. The filter is a shell wildcard pattern (see glob(7)).

parameters.name: filter_out
parameters.description: a pattern used to filter out the active pipes NOT to be listed. The filter is a shell wildcard pattern (see glob(7)).

exported_mi_functions.description:
Lists the parameters and variabiles in the ratelimit module.

Note that you cannot combine multiple paramters when calling this function. If using parameters, only one is accepted.

If no parameter are passed to the function, all the active pipes are listed.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_dump_pipe

parameters.name: pipe
parameters.description: indicates the name of the pipe.

exported_mi_functions.description: Exposes all the details about the current runtime data (specific to the pipe's algorithm) of a pipe. Currently make sense for SBT.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_reset_pipe

parameters.name: pipe
parameters.description: indicates the name of the pipe whose counter should be reset.

exported_mi_functions.description: Resets the counter of a specified pipe.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_set_pid
exported_mi_functions.description: Sets the PID Controller parameters for the Feedback Algorithm.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_get_pid
exported_mi_functions.description: Gets the list of in use PID Controller parameters.

exported_mi_functions.name: rl_bin_status
exported_mi_functions.description: Dumps each destination used for replication, as well as the timestamp of the last message received from them.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $rl_count(name)
exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the counter of a pipe. The variable is read-only. NULL will be returned if the pipe does not exist.
